item.title: Oyebanji seeks FG’s Support To Boost Livestock Development, Job Creation
item.description: Ekiti State Governor, Biodun Oyebanji, is seeking increased support and collaboration from the Federal Government to strengthen livestock development in the state as part of efforts to create more jobs, generate wealth and expand economic opportunities for the people. The Governor appealed on Tuesday while receiving the Minister of Livestock Development, Mallam Idi Mukhtar Maiha, who was in the State to commission an ultra-modern veterinary hospital in Ado Ekiti and inspect ongoing projects of the Livestock Productivity and Resilience Support (LPRESS) across the state. Highlighting the importance of developing the livestock sector to the state’s economic growth, Governor Oyebanji noted that livestock development holds significant potential to boost agricultural productivity, create employment, improve livelihoods, and contribute to the state’s economic development. The Governor stressed the need for a stronger partnership between the state and federal governments to harness opportunities in the sector, particularly through strategic interventions that would strengthen livestock production and the value chain in the state. item.title: CAN disowns cleric, reaffirms neutrality ahead of 2027 polls
item.description: By Luminous Jannamike, Abuja The Christian Association of Nigeria (CAN) has disowned a cleric claiming to represent the association, declaring that he is not its General Secretary and warning against attempts to use its name to mobilise support for political candidates ahead of the 2027 general elections. The association said it had neither authorised the cleric nor the group he represents to organise political activities in its name, stressing that their actions and political positions should not be mistaken for CAN’s official position. In a statement by its president, Archbishop Daniel Okoh, the association identified Archbishop Chivir Chianson as the individual in question, insisting that he had no mandate to speak or act on its behalf and that his group had no official affiliation or institutional relationship with CAN. “For the avoidance of doubt, Archbishop Chivir Chianson is not the General Secretary of CAN and has no authority or mandate to speak or act on its behalf. Furthermore, the group he represents has no official affiliation, working relationship or institutional connection with CAN,” the statement said. CAN warned that it would not allow individuals or groups without official ties to the association to appropriate its identity to advance political or personal interests. The association also reaffirmed its commitment to political neutrality ahead of the 2027 elections, insisting that it would neither endorse candidates nor mobilise support for any political party. “CAN will continue to engage national issues objectively and hold political leaders accountable, irrespective of party affiliation, without endorsing or mobilising support for any political party or candidate,” Archbishop Okoh said. The association urged Christians, members of the public and media organisations to disregard claims of official representation by the cleric and his group. It urged media organisations to verify the credentials and institutional affiliations of individuals presented as CAN representatives. CAN warned that it would take appropriate steps to protect its name, identity and institutional integrity against unauthorised representation and misrepresentation. item.title: Ebonyi Issues 30-Day Ultimatum For Occupants To Vacate Defective Building
item.description: The Ebonyi State Government, through the Ministry of Capital City and Urban Planning, has issued a 30-day ultimatum to occupants of a structurally defective building located at No. 10 Aguluezechukwu Street, Abakaliki, directing them to vacate the premises due to severe structural safety concerns. The order followed an on-site assessment led by the Commissioner for Capital City and Urban Planning, Richard Ugo Idike, alongside the Head of the Town Planning Department, Esther Nwite, state town planners, and the ministry’s enforcement taskforce. During the inspection, Idike expressed deep concern over visible structural defects and substandard construction, describing the building as an immediate threat to life and property. “The state government will not compromise on the safety of residents. Our ministry remains committed to ensuring that all structures across Ebonyi State strictly adhere to approved building codes and regulatory standards,” Idike stated. He explained that the 30-day window provides the property owner time to undertake necessary structural remediation to prevent a catastrophic collapse, while giving occupants sufficient lead time to secure alternative accommodation. “This notice is necessary to avert building failure and protect human lives. Occupants must make alternative arrangements before the expiration of the deadline to avoid tragic outcomes,” the Commissioner added. Idike emphasised that the ministry will step up monitoring and enforcement across the capital to detect unsafe structures, warning that non-compliant properties will face swift regulatory intervention. The exercise aligns with the urban renewal and public safety mandate of the Ebonyi State Government under Governor Francis Ogbonna Nwifuru to maintain an orderly and secure capital city. The Ministry’s Taskforce Team urged property owners, developers, and builders across the state to strictly follow approved building plans, engage certified professionals, and use high-grade construction materials to prevent structural failures. Occupants of the affected property are expected to comply fully with the vacate order within the stipulated 30-day period. item.title: The Politics Of Togetherness And The Trouble With Unity
item.description: As Nigeria’s presidential campaigns gather momentum, political alliances are becoming increasingly difficult to explain. Opponents are finding common ground, party boundaries are becoming less predictable, and the opposition’s search for unity is colliding with the ambitions of its leading figures. But beneath the manoeuvring lies a more consequential question: what exactly are these alliances being formed to achieve? There is something rather fascinating about Nigerian politics. Two politicians can spend the morning attacking each other’s parties, meet for lunch to discuss a common political interest, and appear at an evening gathering celebrating their newfound understanding. By the following morning, both may be insisting that nothing has changed. Welcome to the politics of 2027. This week, the contradictions have become particularly striking. In one corner, politicians from different parties are celebrating their cooperation. In another, opposition figures who profess a common purpose are struggling to agree on how to pursue it. And somewhere between these competing arrangements sits the Nigerian voter, trying to work out who stands for what. That, perhaps, is where today’s Signal begins. Wike And The Unusual Coalition Federal Capital Territory Minister Nyesom Wike has never been particularly troubled by political contradictions. A prominent figure in the Peoples Democratic Party, he serves in an administration led by the All Progressives Congress. He has repeatedly defended his political choices, arguing that cooperation across party lines is not necessarily inconsistent with his political identity. Now, he is drawing attention to what he describes as the unity of APC and PDP leaders, while dismissing criticism of his political relationships. His latest remarks, reported today, come as political alignments continue to shift across several states. The interesting question is not whether Wike is entitled to cooperate with politicians outside his party. Of course he is. The more important question concerns what such cooperation means for the parties themselves. If leading members of rival parties work together to advance shared electoral interests, what becomes of the distinctions between their political organisations? Are these arrangements built around policies, principles and programmes? Or are they primarily agreements between influential individuals? Cross-party cooperation can serve legitimate democratic purposes. Governments frequently need support beyond their own parties, and political compromise is not inherently objectionable. But cooperation becomes harder for voters to interpret when the political objectives and responsibilities of the participants are left unexplained. Wike’s political relationships therefore raise a wider question about the changing character of Nigerian party politics. item.title: Democrat Abdul El-Sayed becomes first Muslim elected US senator
item.description: Democrat Abdul El-Sayed won Michigan’s US Senate race over former Republican lawmaker Mike Rogers, US networks said early Wednesday, making him the first Muslim elected to the upper chamber of Congress. “Michigan, we did it!” El-Sayed said in a speech attended by hundreds of supporters who screamed and hugged each other at his election headquarters in Detroit. “I am so proud and honored to stand here as your senator-elect from the great state of Michigan.” El-Sayed won despite a last-minute curve ball in his campaign when congresswoman Haley Stevens, who lost the Democratic primary to El-Sayed, came out in support of Rogers at the 11th hour. The Michigan medical administrator rallied voters on leftist campaign promises, including universal health care, to win a key US Senate seat for Democrats, taking over from the retiring Gary Peters. El-Sayed held a nearly six-point lead on Rogers when networks called the race. “We are sick and tired of being sick and tired. And I’m so proud of all the work. It was boots on the ground. We were always out, but we were never outworked,” said party-goer entrepreneur Trunetta Roach, 75, who attended El-Sayed’s victory party in downtown Detroit wearing US flag-design diamante high-heels. “I’m feeling elated. The kids are all right. I was concerned about them. They didn’t seem very engaged, but I was wrong. They showed up.” – ‘Swear me in’ – Republicans ran a scorched-earth campaign to paint Democrats as communists and branded El-Sayed a terrorist who would endanger Americans. But the straight-talking 42-year-old El-Sayed pledged to help cash-strapped voters navigate America’s fractured, for-profit health care system. “You deserve to be able to see a doctor without getting a huge bill,” he told Michiganders on the eve of the vote, vowing to upend America’s divisive multi-billion-dollar for-profit medical system. During the race, El-Sayed drew huge campaign crowds across the state, even in deeply conservative Republican areas. El-Sayed also vowed to get “money out of politics” and address the harsh economic woes that have voters yearning for a political newcomer to shake up the status quo. The victory made El-Sayed the first Democratic doctor in the Senate since 1969. “Everybody in politics is so trash. So to see ethical Muslims be at the forefront representing us and showing everybody what we’re actually about… it means everything,” said micro-influencer Maryam Bozai, 28. At the victory party, crowds gathered around TVs tuned to left-leaning cable news channel MS NOW, cheering jubilantly each time the Democrat’s trademark blue flashed on screen to announce another race won by the party. “Tsunami! Tsunami!” chanted Ondine Fortune, 64, a Democratic Party media planner. El-Sayed supporters rubbed shoulders with left-leaning influencers and union activists, a group that lent El-Sayed their formidable campaign infrastructure to reach Michigan’s large organized labor community. item.title: 2027: Tinubu will win second term based on achievements – Alausa
item.description: The Minister of Education, Tunji Alausa, has expressed confidence that President Bola Tinubu will win re-election in 2027, saying his administration’s achievements will secure him a second term. Alausa, recently appointed Director of Education Sector Mobilisation of the All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential Campaign Council, said opposition parties lacked a clear agenda for Nigerians. He made the remarks on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Tuesday, accusing opposition politicians of being motivated by envy and lacking the capacity to govern. “Whatever nonsense these people (opposition) are talking about is out of sheer envy. They can’t deliver, they have been tested, they have no clue of what to do for Nigerians,” Alausa said. “This president is giving Nigerians tangible benefits. Let’s be objective, that is what we have said and I am very unapologetic about this, President Bola Ahmed Tinubu will win his second term squarely based on his achievements.” The minister said Tinubu had transformed different sectors of the economy and deserved another term based on his administration’s performance. “President Bola Ahmed Tinubu has transformed every sector of this country and he deserves to be re-elected come January 16, 2027, based on his accomplishments,” he said. Alausa urged Nigerians to disregard opposition parties, accusing them of seeking to create divisions rather than offer a viable alternative to the ruling APC. “And please, let’s not listen to the opposition parties, they don’t have any clear agenda for this country. They are just there to cause division amongst us,” he added. The minister also cited the Federal Government’s relationship with the Academic Staff Union of Universities (ASUU) as evidence of Tinubu’s achievements in the education sector. According to him, the administration has fulfilled its agreement with the union and is making progress towards ensuring that university students complete their programmes within the stipulated four-year period. Alausa said Tinubu’s commitment to preventing four-year university programmes from extending beyond their duration was being fulfilled. He also noted that ASUU had not embarked on a strike since Tinubu assumed office, presenting the development as evidence of improved relations between the government and university lecturers. item.title: Meet Keisha Lance Bottoms, first black woman elected Governor of US State
item.description: Democrat Keisha Lance Bottoms has made history after winning Georgia’s gubernatorial election, becoming the first Black woman elected governor of a US state. Bottoms, a former mayor of Atlanta, defeated Republican businessman Rick Jackson in Tuesday’s election, according to projections by US media, securing a landmark victory for Democrats in one of the country’s most closely contested political battlegrounds. The 56-year-old will also become Georgia’s first female governor, succeeding Republican Brian Kemp, who is leaving office after serving two consecutive terms. Beyond her political career in Georgia, Bottoms previously served as a senior adviser to former US President Joe Biden and director of the White House Office of Public Engagement. Her victory represents a significant milestone for Black women in American politics, who have historically played an important role in the Democratic Party but remain underrepresented in the country’s highest elected positions. Bottoms’ achievement came on the same night Stacey Plaskett was elected governor of the US Virgin Islands, becoming the first Black woman to lead a US jurisdiction. In Florida, Republican US Representative Byron Donalds also won the governorship, making him the first Black Republican elected governor in the United States. Bottoms’ victory marks a major political shift in Georgia, where Black voters have formed a central part of the Demo cratic coalition that helped transform the traditionally Republican state into a national electoral battleground. Republicans had controlled Georgia’s governorship for more than two decades before her election. Her Republican opponent, Jackson, is a billionaire businessman and founder of healthcare staffing company Jackson Healthcare. He campaigned as a political outsider, promising tax cuts, improved public safety and reduced government regulation. Bottoms’ emergence as governor comes eight years after fellow Democrat Stacey Abrams became the first Black woman nominated for governor by a major US political party. Although Abrams lost Georgia’s gubernatorial elections in 2018 and 2022, her campaigns helped build a multigenerational and multiracial coalition that increased Democratic voter participation. The mobilisation also contributed to the election of two Democratic US senators and helped deliver Georgia’s electoral votes to a Democratic presidential candidate for the first time in decades. Bottoms’ election now adds another chapter to the growing representation of Black women in American political leadership. item.title: ‘Americans want unity, not division’ – Obama reacts to Democrats’ midterm victory
item.description: Former United States President Barack Obama has reacted to the Democratic Party’s sweeping victory in the midterm elections, saying Americans have called for unity and leaders capable of providing practical solutions to the country’s challenges. Obama made the remarks in a statement shared on his official X account on Wednesday, congratulating Democratic candidates who secured victories across different regions of the country. He said the election results reflected Americans’ desire for a political culture that prioritises bringing people together rather than deepening divisions. “Tonight, the American people sent a clear message — they want a politics that brings people together rather than divides them, and leaders who offer concrete solutions to the challenges they face,” he wrote. The former president attributed the party’s success to candidates who contested elections across the country, including in constituencies previously considered difficult for Democrats to win. According to him, the candidates came from diverse backgrounds and represented different political perspectives but shared a commitment to public service and the interests of their constituents. “These results were only possible because outstanding candidates stepped forward in every region of the country — including in areas once considered long shots,” Obama said. He also acknowledged the contributions of election officials and volunteers from both political parties, commending them for ensuring a smooth electoral process. “We also owe a debt of gratitude to the thousands of election officials and volunteers from both parties who helped ensure a smooth election and carried out one of the most essential functions of our democracy,” he added. Despite the Democratic victory, Obama noted that the administration would remain in office for another two years, urging party members to use their newly secured legislative influence to advance changes and limit further damage. “While this administration has another two years in office, our job now is to roll up our sleeves, make changes wherever we have the power to do so, prevent further damage, and lay the groundwork for the future,” he said. The Democrats’ midterm victory is expected to give the party greater control over the legislative process, including congressional investigations, spending negotiations and scrutiny of President Donald Trump’s administration. The outcome could also shape the final two years of Trump’s presidency, as Democrats prepare to challenge several of his policies and exercise their oversight powers in Congress. item.title: Democrats’ Midterm Blowout: The Numbers Behind The Win
item.description: Opposition Democrats stormed back to power in Congress and governors’ mansions across the United States of America in Tuesday’s midterm elections, a stunning repudiation of President Donald Trump’s political agenda. These are the numbers that tell the tale of a historic night. Record Turnout Total turnout numbers were not in yet, but Americans cast more than 61.7 million votes even before election day, according to the University of Florida’s Election Lab. That figure, a runaway record for early voting in US midterms, undoubtedly boosted Democrats, who traditionally cast their ballots early more often than Republican voters. People wait in line to vote on Election Day during the midterm elections at the University of Michigan in Ann Arbor, Michigan, on November 3, 2026. Photo by JEFF KOWALSKY / AFP The numbers showed large turnout among African Americans, young people, and other groups that typically support Democratic candidates, National Public Radio reported. The surge contributed to a wave election, with Democrats running the table on key races and seizing control of both chambers of Congress. People cast their vote on Election Day during the midterm elections at Glenville High School in Cleveland, Ohio, on November 3, 2026. Photo by DAVID MAXWELL / AFP Record Fundraising Total spending for the 2026 midterms soared to a record $11.9 billion, substantially higher than the $8.9 billion racked up in 2022, according to OpenSecrets, a non-partisan authority on spending in US politics. Campaign fundraising and ad buys jumped in the 2026 races, driven by the outside spending of so-called political action committees. Such outside spending, led by Trump’s mega-billionaire ally Elon Musk, favored Republicans by some $360 million. But Democratic candidates proved adept at raising their own funds. House and Senate candidates spent an unprecedented $3.7 billion from their campaign war chests, with Democrats outspending Republicans by $800 million, according to OpenSecrets. In Texas, Democratic Senate candidate James Talarico broke records by bringing in a staggering $145 million, several times the $22 million raised by his Republican rival Ken Paxton, who was forced to rely on outside groups to fund his campaign. First Wins In Decades Ninety-four years ago was the last time Kansas sent a Democrat to the US Senate. But on Tuesday night, Adam Hamilton unseated Republican incumbent Roger Marshall. Hamilton, the pastor of a Methodist megachurch who was registered as a Republican until recently, became the first Democrat to win a Senate race in the largely rural, conservative state since 1932. Texas also went blue for the first time in decades, with Talarico scoring a massive upset to flip a Senate seat in the Lone Star State for the first time since 1988 — the year before Talarico was born. item.title: North Korea’s Kim vows to build ‘most advanced’ warships
item.description: North Korean leader Kim Jong Un vowed to possess “the most advanced and powerful warships” while touring a shipyard, state media reported Wednesday, as Pyongyang accelerates an ambitious naval expansion. Kim toured the Nampho Shipyard on Monday, where North Korea is building a new warship, the state-run Korean Central News Agency (KCNA) said. The nuclear-equipped country has been rapidly upgrading its navy, commissioning 5,000-tonne destroyers and testing ship-launched missiles, while Kim has pledged to arm the fleet with nuclear weapons and build larger 10,000-tonne warships. Pyongyang says the expansion is needed to counter threats from the United States and South Korea, as North Korea develops weapons designed to extend its military reach beyond its traditionally coastal navy. Kim said the “recently emerging geopolitical environment and the hostile acts of adversaries” demonstrated “the need to possess the most advanced and powerful warships”, according to KCNA. The warship under construction has a “combat system possessing operational capabilities that no other country in the world has”, Kim said, stressing the “significant military importance of this enormous concentration of combat power”. “He (Kim) said this was because we must defend our homeland, guarantee our sovereignty and deter all threats.” Kim expressed “great satisfaction” after inspecting the vessel and said it was “incomparable to the destroyer built last year”. The unprecedented operational capabilities could indicate plans to equip the new ships with “strategic cruise missiles (Hwasal series), tactical nuclear weapons, or ship-to-ship and ship-to-surface missiles”, Lim Eul-chul, professor at the Institute for Far Eastern Studies at Kyungnam University, told AFP. North Korea last year unveiled a 5,000-ton destroyer-class vessel, that experts believe can carry both ship-to-surface and ship-to-air missiles. Kim’s shipyard visit came a day after North Korea test-fired strategic cruise missiles, following a separate test of cluster bomb warheads over the weekend. Separately, Kim’s sister warned the United States on Wedendsay that her country will mount a stronger response to Washington’s “invariable hostile policy” toward Pyongyang. item.title: Democrats to challenge Trump’s policies, launch investigations after midterm election victory
item.description: Democrats are preparing a legislative offensive against US President Donald Trump after their sweeping midterm victory handed them control of both chambers of Congress and the power to challenge his policies, investigate his administration and block his nominees. Emboldened by victories deep in traditional Republican territory, the party is promising swift action on living costs and the war in Iran, while signaling that investigations of alleged abuses and corruption will be a major priority. House Democratic leader Hakeem Jeffries, who is in line to become the first Black speaker when the new Congress takes office in January, vowed to go after what he described as “unprecedented corruption” in the government. “Because if you have people in high office who are so focused on enriching themselves, their family members, their friends, or their donors, then they’re not focused on making life better for the American people,” he said. But Democrats will not have a free hand. Trump retains his veto, while Senate rules allow Republicans to obstruct most legislation. Here are the opportunities — and obstacles — ahead. – First 100 hours – Jeffries has promised an ambitious legislative push in the House’s first 100 hours, focused on affordability — the issue that dominated an election shaped by tariffs, high prices and the Iran war. His priorities include restoring expired Affordable Care Act health insurance subsidies, reversing nearly $1 trillion in Medicaid cuts enacted under Trump, rolling back tariffs and pressing for an end to the conflict, which has sent fuel costs soaring. With majorities in both chambers, Democrats can bring their proposals to votes and take charge of spending negotiations. They could use federal budget deadlines to demand concessions, although confrontations over spending risk government shutdowns. – ‘Lawyer up’ – Oversight may offer an even more immediate means of challenging Trump. Robert Garcia, the Democrat expected to chair the powerful House Oversight Committee, fired off a blunt election-night message to Republicans on social media: “LAWYER UP.” Oregon Senator Ron Wyden was even more concise, posting a single word: “Subpoenas.” With control of committees in both chambers, Democrats can summon officials, demand documents and hold public hearings, potentially putting Trump and his senior aides under intense scrutiny. Likely subjects include the Trump family’s business and cryptocurrency dealings, government contracts involving billionaire Elon Musk, cuts to federal agencies, immigration enforcement and the conduct of the Iran war. Democrats have also signaled interest in the handling of files relating to notorious sex offender Jeffrey Epstein. The administration could resist demands for testimony or documents, triggering court battles. Democrats could pursue Trump’s third impeachment, though party leaders have not committed to doing so. item.title: 5 things to know about Nigerian professor Dapo Akande elected ICJ judge
item.description: Nigerian-born legal scholar Professor Dapo Akande has been elected as a judge of the International Court of Justice (ICJ), marking a significant milestone in his career and a diplomatic victory for the United Kingdom. Dapo Akande, who originally qualified as a lawyer in Nigeria, will serve a minimum nine-year term as one of the 15 judges of the United Nations’ principal judicial organ. His election comes at a time when international law is facing increasing scrutiny, with the ICJ playing a prominent role in resolving disputes between countries and addressing major international legal questions. Akande is an internationally recognised expert in public international law and has advised and represented parties in cases before international courts and tribunals, including the ICJ. Following his election, he expressed gratitude to the countries that supported his candidacy, pledging to discharge his responsibilities independently and impartially. “I am deeply honoured to be elected to the international court of justice. “I am incredibly grateful to all the states that have put their faith in me. I pledge to serve with independence and to deciding cases on the basis of a faithful and impartial application of the law. I look forward to contributing to the ICJ’s vital work in helping to resolve disputes by peaceful means, alongside the other colleagues elected today,” he said. Here are five things to know about the Nigerian-born professor and his new international judicial role. 1. He originally qualified as a lawyer in Nigeria Akande began his legal career in Nigeria, where he obtained his initial professional qualification as a lawyer before building an international reputation in public international law. His Nigerian legal background has remained an important part of his professional journey, which has taken him to some of the most prestigious legal and academic institutions in the world. 2. He is a professor at the University of Oxford Akande is a professor of public international law at the University of Oxford, United Kingdom. He is also a fellow of All Souls College, Oxford, one of the university’s prestigious academic institutions. Through his academic work, he has contributed to the study and development of international law, particularly the legal principles governing relations between countries. 3. His membership reflects his standing as an international legal expert and his involvement in shaping discussions around the rules governing relations between states. 4. item.title: Yamal breaks Mbappe’s record as UCL’s highest-scoring teenager [See top 5]
item.description: Barcelona winger Lamine Yamal has surpassed Real Madrid forward Kylian Mbappé to become the highest-scoring teenager in UEFA Champions League history. The 19-year-old set the new record after scoring in Barcelona’s 3-0 victory over Aston Villa on Tuesday. Yamal capitalised on a defensive error by Villa in the seventh minute at Spotify Camp Nou, curling the ball beyond goalkeeper Zion Suzuki to register his 14th Champions League goal. The goal moved him past Mbappé, who previously held the teenage scoring record with 13 goals in the competition. Although the France international has scored 72 Champions League goals overall, Yamal has now claimed the record after just 37 appearances in Europe’s premier club competition. The Spain international has also established several other milestones in the tournament, including becoming the youngest player to start a Champions League match proper. Yamal achieved that feat at the age of 16 years and 83 days when he made his full European debut against FC Porto. His latest achievement comes after an impressive showing at the 2026 Ballon d’Or awards, where he finished third behind Bayern Munich striker Harry Kane and Mbappé. The Barcelona youngster has also enjoyed a productive start to the new season, recording 13 goals and 11 assists in 15 appearances across all competitions. item.description: Following the conclusion of the 11th phase of terrorism trials at the Federal High Court, Abuja, the federal government said it has secured a total of 2,512 convictions in terrorism-related cases over nine years. National Coordinator of the National Counter Terrorism Centre, Office of the National Security Adviser, Major General Adamu Laka, disclosed this during a press briefing in Abuja on Tuesday. According to him, the latest phase, conducted in October 2026, recorded 791 additional convictions out of 1,069 cases handled across 10 courts. He said the trials demonstrated the government’s commitment to combating terrorism, holding perpetrators and their financiers accountable, and strengthening the administration of justice while upholding the rule of law and the fundamental rights of defendants. The National Coordinator said the judgment showed the seriousness with which Nigeria’s justice system addresses terrorism and affirms that perpetrators, regardless of affiliation, were accountable under the law when criminal responsibility was established beyond reasonable doubt. Major General Laka revealed that among the significant outcomes of this phase was the conviction and sentencing to death of Suleiman Abu, in the case of the Federal Republic of Nigeria versus Suleiman Abu. He said the Federal High Court found him guilty of Boko Haram membership and participation in terrorist attacks on military facilities and civilians, resulting in deaths and serious injuries. He said, “I am therefore pleased to report that the 11th phase of terrorism trials recorded significant outcomes. item.title: Soludo seeks pharmacists’ support against fake drugs
item.description: By Steve Oko Anambra State Governor, Prof. Chukwuma Soludo, has called for stronger collaboration with the Pharmaceutical Society of Nigeria (PSN) to tackle fake drugs, improve healthcare delivery and position the state as a major pharmaceutical hub. Soludo made the call while declaring open the 99th Annual National Conference of the PSN, tagged Ijele 2026, in Awka. Speaking on the theme, “One Health, One Pharmacy: Bridging Knowledge, Practice and Policy for National Impact,” the governor described pharmacists as indispensable partners in building an efficient and sustainable healthcare system. He urged the professional body to work with his administration to enforce standards and sanitise the pharmaceutical sector, particularly by tackling counterfeit medicines and illegal operators posing as licensed pharmacies. Soludo said his administration was consolidating Anambra’s position as a pharmaceutical hub through the development of a pharmaceutical hub in Oba and a Coordinated Wholesale Centre, which he said was expected to be completed early next year. The governor also highlighted his administration’s investments in education and healthcare, saying the provision of free education from kindergarten to secondary school had reduced the state’s out-of-school children rate to 0.25 per cent, which he described as the lowest in the country. He further disclosed that the state had strengthened its primary healthcare system, provided free antenatal services to more than 250,000 beneficiaries and conducted over 950 free caesarean operations for expectant mothers. Earlier, PSN President, Pharm. Ayuba Tanko Ibrahim, commended Soludo for his support for the pharmaceutical profession. Ibrahim described Anambra’s hosting of the conference as the fulfilment of a longstanding commitment and praised the governor’s leadership and vision. He said the conference provided an opportunity to deepen cooperation between the pharmaceutical profession and government towards improving healthcare delivery. item.title: Four Nigerian-Americans win US midterm elections
item.description: Four Nigerian-Americans have won elective positions in the November 3 midterm elections in the United States, while the outcome of another candidate, Segun Adeyina, remained pending in Georgia as votes were being counted. Jawando. Photo: Wusa9 The winners are Will Jawando, Junior Ezeonu, Oye Owolewa and Carol Kazeem, who secured positions in local government and state legislatures across Maryland, Texas, Washington, DC, and Pennsylvania. In Maryland, Jawando, the Democratic candidate, won the race for Montgomery County executive, defeating Republican candidate Esther Wells. Results published by NBC Washington on Wednesday showed Jawando polling 237,383 votes, representing 78.15 per cent, against Wells’s 66,383 votes, or 21.85 per cent, with 72 per cent of the expected votes counted. READ ALSO; US Midterms: Democrats take control of US Congress as voters reject Trump’s Republicans Jawando, who previously served on the Montgomery County Council, is the son of a Nigerian father and an American mother. His Nigerian heritage and political career have featured in reports by The Baltimore Banner and The Washington Post. In Texas, 27-year-old Ezeonu secured a seat in the state House of Representatives for District 101. He had defeated incumbent Chris Turner in the Democratic primary and was the only candidate on the ballot for the November general election after no Republican entered the race. According to his campaign biography, Ezeonu was born in Onitsha, Anambra State, and moved to Texas at the age of two. He was elected to the Grand Prairie City Council in 2021 and later became the city’s youngest mayor pro tempore. Oye Owolewa. Photo: Instagram (@repoyedc) In Washington, DC, Owolewa, the Democratic candidate, won an at-large seat on the District of Columbia Council. Local publication, The 51st, reported that Owolewa secured 69 per cent of the vote, against 21 per cent recorded by independent candidate Elissa Silverman. Owolewa, a pharmacist and son of Nigerian immigrants from Kwara and Osun states, previously served as the District’s elected shadow representative. The position allows its holder to advocate for Washington, DC, statehood but does not confer voting rights in the US Congress. Meanwhile, Kazeem, also a Democrat, retained her seat in the Pennsylvania House of Representatives, representing District 159. The result of Adeyina’s contest in Georgia had yet to be called as of Wednesday, with votes still being counted. item.title: ‘Good Job’, Trump Reacts To Democrats’ Victory, Says Iran War Played Role In Midterm Defeat
item.description: US President Donald Trump had rare praise for rival Democrats on Tuesday, saying they had done a “good job” after they routed his Republican Party in the midterm elections. “I think the Democrats did a good job. I really do. I think they did a good job. They fought hard,” Trump told Fox News, adding that there was a “mood in the air” and that “I shouldn’t feel guilty.” President Donald Trump said he would accept the results of US midterm elections — but quickly sought to shift the blame for the historic rout to his fellow Republicans. Time and again on the campaign trail, the 80-year-old told Republicans to “pretend I’m on the ballot.” That may have been exactly the problem, as voters put Democrats in control of the House and Senate. But Trump has never been one to take the blame, and in his first reaction to the election results Tuesday, he insisted that the Republican Party would have won in a “landslide” if he had actually been running. “I wasn’t on the Ballot and if I was, we would have won IN A LANDSLIDE! Thank you for your attention to this matter,” Trump said in a post on his Truth Social platform. Democratic US Senate candidate James Talarico celebrates with supporters after winning the Texas race during a midterm election night watch party at the Long Center for the Performing Arts in Austin, Texas, on November 3, 2026. Dismissing speculation about whether he would repeat his refusal to accept his 2020 presidential election loss to Joe Biden, Trump later took a conciliatory tone with The New York Times. “I am absolutely willing to accept those results,” he told The New York Times. “We’ll work with the Democrats, and we’ll, you know, look forward to working with them. We’ll probably work something out.” But Trump later gave a hint of what he really intended to do to Democratic attempts at legislating, posting a picture of his trademark red MAGA baseball hat with the single word: “VETO.” There was a bunker mentality in the White House as Trump and his top cabinet members watched the bruising results come in at a reception in the lavish East Room. “The White House mood is defiant,” a White House official told AFP. Some White House staffers dined on take-out from US chain restaurant The Cheesecake Factory — a dig at Democratic former president Barack Obama, who had said Trump’s White House renovations were “looking like Saddam Hussein opened a Cheesecake Factory.” Supporters cheer as Democrat senatorial candidate Roy Cooper speaks during an election night event in Raleigh, North Carolina on November 3, 2026. ‘Buckle Up’ A White House official questioned the quality of Republican candidates for the House and Senate. item.title: Dollar to Naira exchange rate today, November 4, 2026
item.description: The dollar-to-naira exchange rate remains a major focus for businesses, importers and Nigerians seeking to meet their foreign exchange needs on Wednesday, November 4, 2026. The Nigerian naira trades against the US dollar at different rates across the Nigerian Foreign Exchange Market (NFEM) and the parallel market, also known as the black market. The NFEM rate reflects transactions in the official foreign exchange market, while the parallel market rate is influenced by demand and supply among independent currency dealers. As of Wednesday morning, the dollar is quoted at approximately ₦1,380 for buying and ₦1,390 for selling in the parallel market. The latest reported official NFEM rate is approximately ₦1,346.43 per dollar, based on the November 3 market publication. In the parallel market, Bureau De Change operators offer different rates depending on location, dollar availability and transaction volume. The quoted buying and selling rates are therefore indicative and may change throughout the day. At the prevailing rates, $100 is worth approximately ₦134,643 at the official market rate and ₦139,000 at the parallel-market selling rate. The difference between the official and parallel-market selling rates is approximately ₦43.57 per dollar. Meanwhile, the naira’s performance in the official market remains influenced by foreign exchange supply, demand from importers and other market participants, and liquidity conditions. Nigerians are advised to confirm prevailing rates with their banks and authorised Bureau De Change operators before conducting foreign exchange transactions, as rates may fluctuate during the day. item.title: Atiku to flag off ADC presidential campaign in Sokoto
item.description: By Musa Ubandawaki, Sokoto Former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar, presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), is expected to visit Sokoto on Wednesday, November 4, 2026, to flag off the party’s presidential campaign activities in the state ahead of the 2027 general elections. Atiku is scheduled to arrive at the Sultan Abubakar III International Airport, Sokoto, at 9 a.m., where party supporters, political associates and members of the public are expected to receive him. The Coordinator of the Sokoto State ADC Presidential Campaign Council, Senator Ibrahim Lamido, disclosed this in a statement made available to journalists. According to the statement, the visit is part of the party’s efforts to strengthen its grassroots structures and consolidate support ahead of the 2027 presidential election. It called on party members, supporters and well-meaning residents to turn out in large numbers to welcome the ADC presidential candidate. The statement said the visit would also feature the flag-off of the party’s presidential campaign in Sokoto State at its secretariat, located at No. 1, Ilorin Road, Sokoto. The event is expected to attract party leaders, elected and appointed political office holders, local government and ward executives, mobilisation coordinators, support groups and other stakeholders. Lamido said local government and ward executives had been directed to activate their political structures and mobilise members and supporters across the state. Women and youth organisations, as well as affiliated support groups, were also urged to intensify grassroots mobilisation and participate actively in the event. The campaign council further called on mobilisation coordinators to ensure effective coordination among the party’s structures to guarantee a successful reception and campaign flag-off. Atiku’s visit comes amid increasing political activities and realignments ahead of the 2027 general elections, as political parties step up efforts to expand their support bases. The statement, however, did not provide further details of the presidential candidate’s engagements during the visit. item.title: Sanusi credits Tinubu for rescuing Nigeria’s economy from brink
item.description: The Emir of Kano, Muhammadu Sanusi II, has said President Bola Tinubu deserves credit for bringing Nigeria’s economy back from the brink, citing improvements in economic growth, inflation, foreign reserves and export diversification. Sanusi, however, cautioned that significant economic challenges remain, saying the country must sustain its current growth trajectory to achieve lasting stability. The former Governor of the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) spoke on Tuesday at the Oxford Global Think Tank conference convened by Arunma Oteh. “I’m not a fan of politicians, but we need to give credit to President Tinubu’s administration for bringing us back from the brink,” he said. Sanusi cited the country’s economic growth of 4.48 per cent in the second quarter of 2026, describing it as an improvement over the average performance recorded during the administration of former President Muhammadu Buhari. “GDP in Q2 2026 was at 4.48 percent. It’s not as high as it was under the Yar’Adua/Jonathan government, but during the Buhari years, the economy grew by 0.9 percent. Today it’s at 4.5 percent. That’s progress,” he said. He also highlighted the decline in inflation from about 30 per cent to 14.6 per cent, noting that it was projected to fall further to 12.5 per cent by the end of the year. On economic growth and living standards, the emir said Nigeria’s gross domestic product (GDP) per capita, measured in dollar terms, had increased by 47 per cent since 2023. He expressed optimism that sustaining the current pace of growth could restore the country’s GDP per capita to its 2005 level by the end of next year. “If we continue at this rate, by the end of next year, GDP per capita will be back to where it was in 2005,” he said. Sanusi also pointed to Nigeria’s foreign reserves, which he put at $55 billion, but warned that a substantial portion of the inflows was driven by foreign portfolio investments, which could be volatile. “Our reserves are at $55 billion, and yes, a lot of it is driven by portfolio flows, which are volatile,” he said. He attributed the continued inflows partly to high oil prices amid the conflict in the Strait of Hormuz and attractive returns available to investors in Nigeria. On export diversification, Sanusi said 20 per cent of Nigeria’s exports were coming from the Dangote Refinery, describing the development as evidence of progress beyond the country’s traditional export sources. Despite acknowledging the economic gains, the former CBN governor criticised the Tinubu administration’s communication strategy, saying the government appeared to interpret criticism and constructive suggestions as attacks. “This government doesn’t express itself properly. It sees every suggestion and contribution it does not like as an attack, and it doesn’t have good spokespersons,” he said. item.title: Experts push renewables to tackle Nigeria’s power crisis
item.description: By Udeme Akpan Power sector experts have called for accelerated deployment of renewable energy and microgrids to address Nigeria’s persistent electricity supply challenges and reduce dependence on the national grid. Speaking in separate interviews with Vanguard at the recently concluded Nigeria Energy Summit in Lagos, they said decentralised power solutions would improve electricity access, particularly for businesses and rural communities. Product Manager, DEIF, Anshul Alankar, said: “The reality is that renewable energy is the in-thing, and government policy also supports it. It is important to latch on to it as early as possible, especially for the commercial sector and even for individual users. “The grid system is not able to provide all the electricity and power needed by Nigerians and Africans to maintain sustainable energy. “Nigeria has surplus solar energy, and microgrids will help because you don’t need huge infrastructure to bring power across the country. “Microgrids are a more efficient way of handling local and rural areas. You can create your own grid, minimise fuel consumption and maximise the sun, which is free.” On the growing demand for decentralised energy, he said: “We see that the need of the market is around microgrids and fuel efficiency. We provide solutions that enable batteries to work more efficiently and solar panels to be maximised.” Also speaking, Executive Director, Delmira Power Solutions, Dr. Moriam Jagun, said the company was bringing advanced power management solutions into Nigeria. She said its technologies “coordinate, protect and monitor energy, making sure that energy is efficiently generated and delivered, both for land and marine.” Sales Head, Engineering, Delmira Power Solutions, Engr. Nmecha Chizinum Ayodele, said: “Our country has come to the point of further expansion in renewable energy, from household to grid levels.” He added: “DEIF solutions can remotely monitor, automate and synchronise different power sources to provide all-round power for industries and homes, thereby reducing the cost of energy.” The post Experts push renewables to tackle Nigeria’s power crisis appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: US Midterm: Democrats Retake Congress In Major Blow Against Trump’s Republicans
item.description: Democrats won full control of the US Congress in a sweeping midterm rout Tuesday with a landslide of upsets that delivered a crushing rebuke of President Donald Trump and his Republican Party. The victory handed Democrats both the House of Representatives and Senate, giving them power to block Trump’s agenda and investigate alleged corruption for the last two years of his presidency. The vote reflected deep anger over living costs, tariffs and Trump’s war against Iran, which has sent fuel prices soaring and compounded dissatisfaction with an already deeply unpopular president. Trump struck a conciliatory note despite his history of questioning election results, telling The New York Times: “I am absolutely willing to accept those results” and promising to “work with the Democrats.” But minutes later on social media, the 80-year-old signaled how he intends to deal with Democratic attempts to pass laws, posting a picture of a red baseball cap emblazoned: “VETO.” The Democrats’ decisive Senate breakthroughs came in Kansas and Iowa, the fifth and sixth Republican-held seats to fall in the extraordinary “blue wave” election night. In Kansas, Methodist minister Adam Hamilton defeated Republican incumbent Roger Marshall, becoming the first Democrat elected to the Senate from the reliably conservative state since 1932. Iowa had not elected a Democratic senator since 2008, again illustrating the scale of the party’s inroads into Republican strongholds. The upsets followed victories in Texas, South Carolina, North Carolina and Ohio, where voters rejected Republican candidates despite Trump’s intensive efforts to rally his supporters. Texas was a political bombshell. Democrat James Talarico ousted a Trump-backed Senate candidate, while Gina Hinojosa unseated Republican governor Greg Abbott, ending decades of Republican control of the state’s top office. Democrats also protected key Senate seats of their own, including Jon Ossoff’s in Georgia and an open seat in New Hampshire. Republicans had held a 53-47 Senate majority. The six-seat Democratic gain proved sufficient for networks to project a takeover despite some races remaining unresolved. Supporters of Democratic US Senate candidate James Talarico cheer after he won the Texas race during a midterm election night watch party at the Long Center for the Performing Arts in Austin, Texas, on November 3, 2026. Republican Heartland Democrats also captured the House after flipping Republican-held districts in states stretching from Pennsylvania and New Jersey to Kentucky, Arizona and North Carolina. Some victories came in territory Trump had carried comfortably in 2024, despite Republican attempts to shore up House seats by redrawing electoral boundaries. One bellwether was Indiana, where Democrat J.D. Ford defeated Republican congresswoman Victoria Spartz in a district Trump won by 17 points. item.title: ADC’s struggle to campaign
item.description: There was an air of uncertainty on Tuesday over whether the flag-off of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) presidential campaign in Sokoto State scheduled for Wednesday (today) would be held as planned. Daily Trust gathered that, as of Tuesday evening, the party was still struggling to secure a venue for the event, mobilise supporters, and make other basic logistical arrangements for the rally. Our correspondents report that the event was initially scheduled for Saturday, October 31, but was shifted to Wednesday due to the alleged takeover of hotel bookings by the state government, which has denied the claim. It was learnt that due to problems of logistics, some ADC leaders in the state offered their homes and guest houses to accommodate party leaders and other dignitaries arriving for the party’s presidential campaign flag-off. Benue APC: Rival Tinubu campaign lists deepen factional rift Can the North afford to continue without its own ‘Parapo’? Some party leaders confirmed this in separate interviews with our correspondents, saying they resorted to providing private accommodation after failing to secure hotel rooms for their guests. Spokesman for the ADC governorship candidate in Sokoto State, Aminu Abubakar, said the party was yet to secure hotel accommodation, prompting members to volunteer their residences and guest houses. “Some of them have offered their homes, while others have provided their guest houses to accommodate our visitors. That is where we are putting them up,” he said. Another party chieftain, who spoke on condition of anonymity, said some prominent party leaders had already arrived in Sokoto ahead of the event. He said they include the party’s National Secretary and former Osun State Governor, Rauf Aregbesola; Senator Dino Melaye; and the party’s governorship candidate in Kaduna State, Isa Ashiru Kudan. The source added that more party leaders and dignitaries were expected to arrive Tuesday night or early Wednesday. However, the party was yet to officially announce the exact venue of the rally as of the time of filing this report. Supporters of the ADC in Sokoto yesterday An unverified source claimed that the event would take place at the Trade Fair Complex, while another source said it would be held at the party’s office premises along Ahmadu Bello Way, which was recently sealed by the state government. A source familiar with the arrangement alleged that the party had been asked to pay N20 million for the use of the Trade Fair Complex. According to the source, the party had agreed to the payment and requested the account details to enable it to transfer the money, but the details had yet to be provided. Director-General of the ADC Governorship Campaign Council, Bello Muhammad Goronyo, when contacted for clarification on the arrival of party leaders and the venue of the event declined to comment, saying he was not aware of the arrival of the guests or where the presidential campaign flag-off would take place.
